300.000 years of human evolution, countless scientific advancements, and yet, none of that has come close to the unadulterated mastery of this game. This game has it all, high octane gameplay? Done. High intensity music with hard hitting lyrics that will leave you speechless? Achieved. Deep philosophical and sociological meanings embedded neatly into the gameplay that will undoubtedly affect the forseeable future of our entire existence as a species? Probably not, but the game is FREE! I know what you might be thinking, "This can't be, no one can make something so great and set the price to free! It must be riddled with microtransactions!" well, my dear dearest deer companion, the great minds at chromatophore games are not motivated by money, they are motivated by something far greater, something so elephantinly huge that no AAA gaming company would even DARE to attempt to be motivated by, that thing is called... Making good games. Yes, you heard/read me right, making good games, and this game is one of them good ones. Play it, it's free, doesn't cost anything, and is costless. It might change your life forever, or not! Life is yours to choose after all.

I downloaded Wheelchair Wizards because the idea sounded ridiculous. It somehow ended up being way more fun than I expected. The game fully commits to its absurd premise, and that's what makes it work. Instead of trying to be serious, it embraces the chaos, and every match turns into a mix of skill, bad decisions, and moments that have everyone laughing. It's the kind of game where you'll say, "One more round." An hour later... You're still playing. Not every game needs realistic graphics or a deep story to be memorable. Sometimes all you need is a creative idea that's executed well. I came for the joke. I stayed because it was actually fun. Recommended.

The amount of skill expression possible in this game is genuinely unseen in a great many other games of its type. The amount of instant-speed thinking and strategy that occurs midgame make it a surprisingly complex fighter. The split-second decision of whether to stay with light-life for the range and speed of light's laser attack or to take rock for the defense is one that I made several times in the couple hours I've played so far, and every one of those moment-fast choices either led me to victory or defeat. The game is also programmed surprisingly well, with every spell and movement option working quite well despite terrible wi-fi. Multiple times, while my opponent appeared to have a framerate of 6 for the purposes of their movement, their beam still hit me and my flashbang still perfectly collided with them. The bouncing projectiles and other physics mechanics are also quite well made, and I have not encountered a singe bug with them so far. The game is also well optimised, with my abysmal laptop somehow running it well above 60 fps. Overall, I very much reccomend Wheelchair Wizards. It's fun, fast-paced, surprisingly in-depth, and a delightful experience with a friend or two, and it is certainly worth a whole heck of a lot more than the price of zero dollars and zero cents.
